idea-plugin.name: Terminal Tab Tailor
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New ?

Requirement
  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1 or later: this release drops support for 2024.x. If you are still on 2024.x, version 1.4.3 remains available and keeps working.
Changed
  • Reusing a tab is now the default: opening a terminal for something that already has a matching tab brings that tab back up instead of adding a duplicate. If you preferred the previous behaviour, untick "Reuse an existing tab when the names match" in Settings > Tools > Terminal Tab Tailor.
Fix
  • Unhandled exception in Dispatchers.Default: naming a newly opened terminal tab could raise an IDE error report.

Pro-tip : Enhance your efficiency by assigning a shortcut to the "Open In > Terminal" action.
idea-plugin.description:
Terminal Tab Tailor significantly enhances the IntelliJ IDEA workflow by dynamically renaming terminal tabs to reflect the currently selected item in your project tree. This feature greatly aids in organizing your workspace and navigating effortlessly between numerous terminal sessions.

Simply select a file or folder within your project tree and initiate a terminal session from that context.

Pro-tip: Enhance your efficiency by assigning a shortcut to the "Open In > Terminal" action

Three ways to open a tailored tab
  • Open In > Terminal - Terminal Tab Tailor takes over the IDE's own "Open in Terminal" action, so every place you already open a terminal from produces a tailored tab. There is nothing new to learn.
  • The TTT Button - the "Open in Terminal" action in one click, from the terminal toolbar, using your most recent selection.
  • Rename Session - right-click any tab to name it yourself. Your sort order is re-applied straight away and the renamed tab stays selected.
Choose what the TTT Button follows:
  • Use the last selection from the Project Tree.
  • Use the last selected Tab from the File Editor.
  • Use the most recent selection, whether from the Project Tree or the File Editor Manager.
  • Use the project name, always.
Options & Sort
  • Reuse an existing tab when the names match.
  • Prompt the renaming dialogue each time a new terminal tab is opened.
  • Incorporate the current date into tab names (with a customizable pattern, defaulting to dd-MM-yy).
  • Maintain tabs in perpetual alphabetical order.
  • Maintain tabs sorted by descending date.
  • Do not sort tabs.
Whichever you choose, opening or reusing a tab brings the terminal window to the front and selects that tab.

Choose from a variety of naming conventions to suit your workflow:
  • Permit the use of file names directly.
  • Default to directory names, utilizing the parent directory's name for files.
  • Adopt the name of the parent module.
  • Use the parent module's directory name for a more structured approach.
  • Consistently use the project's name for all terminal tabs.
Configurability is at the heart of Terminal Tab Tailor. Find the settings in Settings > Tools > Terminal Tab Tailor, or via Terminal Tab Tailor Settings in the dropdown next to + in the Terminal tool window.
